questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: A pre-test loop repeats while the destination has not been reached. What makes it stop?
answers: The loop count is always two
questions.explanation: Once the destination is reached, the while condition becomes false.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: A process handles one queued item per iteration until the queue is empty. It starts with 6 items and receives no new items. How many iterations are needed?
questions.explanation: Each iteration removes one of the six starting items.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: Why must a repeat-until rule specify when its condition is checked?
answers: A condition cannot be checked twice
All languages use identical loop semantics
Checking before or after the body can change the first iteration
questions.explanation: Pre-test and post-test loops can behave differently when the condition starts true.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: A loop should stop when remaining <= 0. Why is that safer than remaining == 0 if updates may subtract 2?
answers: It forces the value to stay positive
It also stops when the value skips below zero
questions.explanation: A decrement of two can pass from one to minus one without equaling zero.
